clue.text: Result of www, perhaps? Bird in the third 'w' backed by the first

indicators.note: in tells us the bird goes inside the backwards third word
backed means turned back to front, so the word web is read from its end

parts.note: the third w of www, the World Wide Web, stands for web
a raven is a large black bird
by means next to, and the first w of www stands for world

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what the World Wide Web has brought about, with a bird nesting among its letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Each w of www stands for a word: world, wide, web. 'backed' turns the third round and 'in' puts the bird inside. Huxley's novel title is a playful result of the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Huxley's phrase for a dazzling technological future is what the internet era might be said to have produced.

clue.text: Inverse of reverse in knots

indicators.note: the inverse of a two-word phrase here swaps its two words, putting the first word after the second

parts.note: to reverse is to turn round

explanation.surface: A riddle about opposites of opposites, tied up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inverse of' swaps the two words of TURN ROUND. 'in knots' is a field label: the answer is a term from knotting.
explanation.definitionFit: In knotting and sailing, this is a complete loop of rope taken around a post or ring before securing it.

clue.text: What's gripping about love is the sound

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the gripping tool goes round the letter for love

parts.note: a vice is a clamp that grips work on a bench
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about what holds a lover's attention, answered as a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: One's vocal sound is the noise made when speaking or singing.

clue.text: Sunni reformer with tomb in dream

indicators.note: a reformer re-forms things, so the letters of the sect's name are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A religious reformer from the Sunni tradition with a tomb seen in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Pyramus and Thisbe meet at 'Ninny's tomb', the mechanicals' garbling of the tomb of this legendary Assyrian king; the Dream is the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary founder of Nineveh is the king whose tomb is the lovers' meeting place in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: 25 lover drunk in drink

indicators.note: in places the rearranged lover inside the drink

parts.note: wine is a drink

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of lover reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A greedy person, a lover of food, gets drunk on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. The cross-reference 25 is the first word of 25/26 across, an alternative name for this animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This fierce northern mammal of the weasel family is also known as the glutton for its supposed voracity.

clue.text: Lover of drink from fifty-one, I hope

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters are reworked into the answer

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone fond of wine, hopeful of getting some from a group of fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals an anagram of L, ONE and I HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of wine is literally a wine-lover, from the Greek oinos for wine.

clue.text: Beast putting up a place to shop?

indicators.note: putting up in a down clue means writing the letters upwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: An animal being housed in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' reverses A MALL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid kept for wool and as a pack animal is a beast.

clue.text: Reject motion that's more than 100 years old

parts.note: to scout an idea is to reject it scornfully
a movement is a motion

explanation.surface: Throwing out a proposal that has been around for over a century.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: Baden-Powell's youth organisation dates from 1907-08.
explanation.definitionFit: The youth organisation founded by Baden-Powell began in 1907, so it is over a century old.

clue.text: Do without peas in predilection for plumbism

indicators.note: in places the clothed peas inside the word for a predilection

parts.note: a leaning is a predilection or inclination

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word do goes around the peas

parts.note: pois is French for peas

explanation.surface: Doing without peas because of a fondness for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking, and 'peas' needs French. The result goes 'in' the predilection, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbism is the medical name for toxic illness caused by the metal, from Latin plumbum.

clue.text: Warning: take care of card

definitions.meaning: a warning given, as by a police officer
the one-word exclamation telling someone to be careful
a card is an amusing, eccentric person, a real character

explanation.surface: A warning notice telling the reader to look after a card.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an admonition, an exclamation of 'be careful', and informally an amusing or outrageous person.

clue.text: Dancing years shown in tree

parts.note: line dancing is a type of dancing, so dancing gives line
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: Years of dancing displayed in a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree charts descent, the line of one's ancestry.

clue.text: Too much not owed?

parts.note: un- is a prefix meaning not
a debt that is due is owed

explanation.surface: Asking whether an excessive sum is in fact not owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the word is read literally as 'not due'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive or unwarranted, as in excessive pressure, beyond what is fitting.

clue.text: Second shower from worker on chimney?

definitions.meaning: the clock pointer that shows the seconds
read as a hand, a worker, employed by the man who cleans chimneys

explanation.surface: A second spray of water coming down from someone working on a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' means one that shows, not a spray of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuously moving clock pointer showing seconds, and jokingly the assistant of a chimney cleaner.

clue.text: Fungal pattern

definitions.meaning: an adjective standing for the fungal growth itself, a furry growth on stale food
a pattern or template from which things are shaped

explanation.surface: A design based on fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a furry fungal growth and a hollow form that shapes molten metal or jelly.

clue.text: Not much filthy lucre needed — carpet hid result

indicators.note: a result is what comes out of something, so the letters produce something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A carpet hiding money resulted in a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' signals an anagram of CARPET HID; 'filthy lucre' plays on the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very inexpensive costs hardly any money, which is jokingly called filthy lucre.

clue.text: Backing pieces (new trio is included) played with fire

indicators.note: included means put inside, so the rearranged trio goes within the backwards pieces
backing means running backwards, so ops is read in reverse

parts.note: ops is short for opuses, musical pieces

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Sections of a piece, with a fresh trio added, performed with fiery spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reverses the pieces, 'new' scrambles 'trio is', and 'included' puts that scramble between the second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction asks for a spirited, lively performance.

clue.text: Church officer is missing — emergency: devil about!

indicators.note: about means going around, so the devil surrounds the shortened emergency

parts.note: Satan is the devil

indicators.note: missing means the word is is dropped from the emergency

parts.note: a crisis is an emergency

explanation.surface: A churchman is missing, an emergency because the devil is on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the clue's own 'is' from the emergency, and 'devil about' puts the devil round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton or verger who looks after a church's sacred vessels and vestments is a church official.

clue.text: What 25 has done before a time in cooker

indicators.note: in places the run of short words inside the cooker

parts.note: an oven is a cooker
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: What a greedy eater has done, hours before meal time, at the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 25 is the first word of 25/26 across, a person who eats greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater has consumed too much food, the past participle fitting 'has done'.

clue.text: It is in heart when little flow is uttered by cockney

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, and a stage cockney is imagined saying the w as a v

parts.note: when gives WHEN; a trickle is a little flow of liquid

explanation.surface: Something inside the heart, appearing when a cockney speaks of a small flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The stage cockney here, as in Dickens's Sam Weller, turns W into V, so 'when trickle' comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two lower pumping chambers is a part of the heart.

clue.text: Timeless things that happen by chance

indicators.note: timeless read as time-less, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: events are things that happen

explanation.surface: Eternal things that happen by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' is read as 'T-less': EVENTS without T.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, odds of one to one express an even, fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: I would be hurt if nuts accepted left-wing greeting

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the nuts surround the other pieces

parts.note: mast is the nuts of beech and oak trees
Soc is short for socialist
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Someone would be offended if crazy people welcomed a socialist hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is not madness but MAST, fallen beech nuts. The definition is what the answer would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who enjoys pain would wish to be hurt, so this is a statement such a person makes.

clue.text: Fight between words and music?

definitions.meaning: words are ... music, so the phrase is what joins them

explanation.surface: A quarrel between lyricist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, vigorous fight or argument; also the link in setting lyrics to a tune.

clue.text: European river labelled American?

parts.note: to tag is to label, so labelled gives tag followed by its object

explanation.surface: A river in Europe tagged as American.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'labelled American' as TAG US, tag the American.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river of the Iberian peninsula flows through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.

clue.text: Roisin's reported radiance

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so we hear how part of the name is pronounced

parts.note: the 'sin' ending of the Irish name Roisin is pronounced '...'

explanation.surface: A woman's reported glow.
explanation.walkthrough: Róisín is an Irish girl's name pronounced roughly 'Ro-sheen', so its 'sin' is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft lustre on a surface is a gleam or radiance.

clue.text: Quiet inside with sergeant major outside

indicators.note: outside means the officer's letters go round the inner part

parts.note: tum, the stomach, is one's inside

explanation.surface: A quiet word indoors with a sergeant major standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from German, the word means silent, mute or quiet.

clue.text: A bank where blows wild thyme etc and Titania some night, initially

indicators.note: blows here means is blown about, so the gathered letters are scattered into a new order
initially means take the first letter of each word that follows where

explanation.surface: Oberon's line 'I know a bank where the wild thyme blows', where Titania sleeps some nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes WTEATSN from 'wild thyme etc and Titania some night', and 'blows' scrambles them. 'A bank' is the high-street bank, not Shakespeare's riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of Britain's big high-street banks, National Westminster.

clue.text: Extreme 20 wildly flung net in Portsmouth

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of the phrase are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A net flung wildly in a naval port.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer to 20 across, one who enjoys pain; the whole phrase is an extreme case of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seems to seek out hardship is an extreme case of a person who enjoys being hurt.

clue.text: See 25
